study type: Case series with control group comparison
outcome: Need for intensive care unit care
cohort: The study included 12 pregnancies in 10 women with complete heart block, compared with 24 low-risk pregnancies as controls.
finding: Pregnancy in patients without a permanent pacemaker (PPM) can be safely managed with good obstetric and neonatal outcomes, provided backup for temporary pacemaker implantation (TPI) and/or cardiac interventions is available during labor.
mod_finding: The cesarean delivery rate was higher in patients with CHB (75%) compared to controls (37.5%), although this difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.07).
birth_weight: Mean birth weight was lower among cases (2443 ± 442 g) compared to controls (3167 ± 434 g).
